input.quote: Section 3.6 Review of Servicer's Records. The Servicer will maintain records and documents relating to its performance under this Agreement according to its customary business practices. Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The only audit/review rights in this Agreement run in our favour, not against us. Section 3.6 (p0131) gives the Issuer, Depositor and other transaction parties access to the Servicer's (Cellco's) records, and Section 6.7 (p0303 et seq.) requires the Servicer to deliver annual Regulation AB compliance assessments and a registered public accounting firm's attestation to us; under Section 3.9 (p0135) the Servicer bears its own expenses, including independent accountants' fees, so cost sits with the counterparty. There is no inspection, verification or audit right exercisable by Cellco against Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A or Verizon ABS LLC anywhere in the document (searches for "audit", "inspect", "examine" and "books and records" return nothing adverse), and no remote or direct access to our systems. Nothing to flag under this rule. Noted only (not a deviation, and in any event a limit on rights we hold): our Section 3.6 access is capped at once per calendar year on "reasonable notice", must be exercised by all parties simultaneously at the Servicer's offices, and is subject to the Servicer's own security, confidentiality, privacy and data-protection policies — customary for a securitisation servicing agreement, but it is the counterparty rather than an independent auditor that controls the conditions of access.
